newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Controls sees more controls growth.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Controls sees more controls growth.

text.p: Johnson Controls Inc said on Thursday it expects double-digit growth to continue for its controls businesses as non-residential building owners continue to look for ways to reduce energy and operating costs.

The company, which posted improved results for the fourth quarter and full year ended September 30, said controls sales for fiscal 1996 increased 13 percent to $2.96 billion from $2.63 million the prior year, while operating income advanced 12 percent to $118.6 million.

Sales of systems and services worldwide rose about 10 percent, reflecting strength in the existing buildings market in North America and Europe, while a high level of new construction boosted results from the Asia/Pacific region.
The company said that orders for systems and services worldwide also rose by about 10 percent.

Johnson Controls said its automotive business sales rose 35 percent to $5.31 billion with two-thirds of the increase due to internal growth and one-third reflected in the 1996 acquisition of Roth Freres, a French seating and interior systems company.

It said the internal growth stemmed from the company's new seating programs for vehicles such as the Ford Motor Co F-Series light truck in North America and the Ford Fiesta car in Europe. The sales increase came despite relatively flat vehicle production levels in North America and Europe.

Johnson Controls said plastics sales fell 11 percent in fiscal 1996 to $968 million. The company said the revenue decline primarily stemmed from the pass-through of lower resin prices to customers worldwide and cooler than average summer temperatures in North America and Europe.

Unit shipments were slightly higher than a year ago as higher unit demand for water and single- serve bottles offset lower shipments of two-liter bottles. Operating income decreased 62 percent to $24.0 million from $63.6 million a year ago due to competitive pressures, declining resin prices and unabsorbed manufacturing capacity resulting from the weaker than anticipated market demand.
The company said battery sales rose 15 percent to $774 million. Unit shipments of automotive batteries to the replacement and original equipment markets were more than 10 percent higher.
Earlier, Johnson Controls reported fourth-quarter earnings per diluted share rose to $1.79 from $1.46. For the full year, earnings per diluted share were $5.10, up from $4.27.
